title: Solid multitasking device
content: The base level iPad is a surprisingly competent device for casual use and the occasional work session. I have a gaming laptop for my regular machine so this is a welcome addition to my desk, especially with the Apple Pencil. < Pros > Very fast A12 mobile chip, it powers through websites like they're nothing. The screen is sharp and clear - I'm not sure what 2160x1620 is considered, but I'd say somewhere between 1080p and Quad HD. Colors are super bright, but blacks are lackluster. 3GB RAM allows for some multitasking! Apple Pencil is absolutely necessary (and fantastic) for artists or people who prefer to hand-write their notes. Build quality is fantastic, but this is Apple. Did you expect anything else? The speakers are great. Bass is prevalent. The rear camera is pretty high-quality and useful for taking pictures of documents to electronically write on. < Cons > 10.2" screen/4:3 ratio and the aforementioned 3GB RAM limits how much you can multitask. 32GB of storage is unacceptable in today's world. Consider getting more Google Drive or iCloud storage, or buying the 128GB model. Accessories are WILDLY expensive. I ended up getting the Apple Pencil used and an off-brand keyboard called Typecase. (BTW, Typecase is more versatile, better, and cheaper than any Apple keyboard.) There's no convenient place to store the Apple Pencil like on the newer iPads. Lightning charging is the bane of my existence. I wish they'd just go with USB-C. The webcam is atrocious and badly placed. Landscape mode would be ideal for teleconferencing. This may seem like a lot of cons, but the pros outweigh them, especially for the price. If you can afford the Air, go for the Air, but if you're strapped for cash like me, definitely check this out.

title: Nice tablet, but Apple sure doesn't make it easy on their customers...
content: Because I got tired of replacing my Kindle Fires every time they get slow, I opted to give iPad a try. It's not easy to set-up unless you're an "Apple person" and already have an Apple ID, credit card on file, etc. The "go back" arrow is always at the very top of the screen in any app, so you've got to take your hand off holding the thing to touch the arrow--it should have been on the bottom. Using the Kindle app is almost impossible unless every ebook you own was purchased from Amazon. You cannot load ebooks from your PC to the iPad's Kindle app because Apple has taken the "Apps" button off iTunes. In years past, clicking on Apps in iTunes would open up an iPad Kindle window and you could drag your books to the Kindle App. Not anymore. The only way to do it is to email the book to the kindle address assigned to your Kindle App by Amazon and I don't think it's any of Amazon's business what ebooks I have that didn't come from them. Likewise, Calibre E-book Management software doesn't work with the iPad's build-in e-book reader unless you want to convert every book you want to read to EPUB format. Calibre cannot move a MOBI book to the Kindle App on the iPad. Additionally, while you CAN connect the iPad to a PC, all you're going to have access to is the DCIM folder, so you cannot move any files where they need to go. Apple also forces you to use iTunes to move any music to the iPad--you can't just drag and drop from Windows Explorer. Again, nice tablet, but Apple does their level best to make it hard on you if you use a PC instead of a Mac.

If you don't care about specs or minor details, I'm 99% sure you'll be happy with this tablet. If you're capable of spending a lot of money on a really nice tablet and being very critical, buy an iPad Pro! But if you're like me just looking for something that works well enough, this is the perfect choice. I was a little worried about buying it from Amazon instead of Apple, but it arrived faster than its estimated date, came in all of its original packaging, and works wonderful! It's what you'd expect from Apple: it runs very smoothly and it's user friendly. The camera quality is mediocre at best but I doubt you're looking at tablets for stellar camera action. The speakers are quite impressive in my opinion, there's touch ID on the home button, and the fact it has a headphone jack makes me very happy. All and all, highly recommend this tablet! It works great for making art and just general entertainment :]
